I am writing this note to express my gratitude to all the readers who have supported us over the years.

I think it is a miracle that it lasted for 12 years as a media outlet with almost no advertising and a non-profit nature. I have nothing but gratitude for our readers and all the people involved in its operation.
Six months after the launch, the site's PV had gradually increased, but it had not reached the goals set at the beginning of the project.

Thanks to the buzz, once our monthly PV exceeded 100,000, we gained recognition within the industry, and requests for interviews and introductions of pre-release products began to increase. I finally felt that we had become a "media-like" presence. In the end, we grew to 1 million PV/month combined with our sister site, "fabcross for Engineers."

From the beginning, fabcross has maintained an editorial policy of intentionally mixing serious interviews and news articles with somewhat playful craft topics. Since the fields we cover are niche, both our information sources and readership are limited. Therefore, the goal was to attract many users with topical craft projects while also having them read serious articles.

Looking back, I believe this kind of sales activity was extremely important for developing sources for interviews. After becoming independent, I have sometimes helped with content marketing and owned media management, and I have the impression that media outlets whose representatives do not show their faces to interviewees struggle to grow.

Thanks to the buzz, once our monthly PV exceeded 100,000, we gained recognition within the industry, and requests for interviews and introductions of pre-release products began to increase. I finally felt that we had become a "media-like" presence. In the end, we grew to 1 million PV/month combined with our sister site, "fabcross for Engineers."

As access numbers approached current levels, requests for advertorials began to pour in, either directly or through referrals. We accepted these projects as much as possible to secure revenue for the media. Since we were operating as a business at the time, sales were one of our KPIs.

On the other hand, from this time on, I was blessed with connections to talented creators, and we were able to develop regular craft projects. Since we could also expect ripple effects for PR projects and events, advertising sales began to emerge around 2014, and we even had one month where we were in the black.

fabcross was launched in 2013 as a new business by Meitec, an engineer staffing company, and after many twists and turns, it was later operated as an advertising tool for branding and employee recruitment.

I think it is a miracle that it lasted for 12 years as a media outlet with almost no advertising and a non-profit nature. I have nothing but gratitude for our readers and all the people involved in its operation.

On the other hand, from this time on, I was blessed with connections to talented creators, and we were able to develop regular craft projects. Since we could also expect ripple effects for PR projects and events, advertising sales began to emerge around 2014, and we even had one month where we were in the black.

Recently, I have heard from colleagues in the industry that media articles are no longer shared on social media, the center of web media is shifting from text to video, and the number of people aspiring to be writers is only decreasing. With the advertising business also changing significantly, I feel that the way text-based media is operated has changed greatly from 10 years ago.

On the Closure of fabcross
The web media "fabcross," which had been in operation since 2013, will be closed as of March 31, 2025.
I was honestly surprised that it was picked up by ITmedia and Internet Watch.
I am writing this note to express my gratitude to all the readers who have supported us over the years.

Normally, something like this should be posted on fabcross, but since the cloud server used by fabcross will also be canceled at the end of March (meaning all articles will become inaccessible), I have uploaded it here instead.

fabcross was launched in 2013 as a new business by Meitec, an engineer staffing company, and after many twists and turns, it was later operated as an advertising tool for branding and employee recruitment.

While it was in a form close to what is known as an owned media, we operated it with a policy of conveying information neutrally, updating it every weekday, and maintaining a structure no different from a general web media. We maintained careful content creation from the beginning, which is rare for recent web media, such as having a proofreader separate from the editorial staff.
